sections.content: This policy establishes baseline information security practices for M004 policy-eval corpus - Four-person fully remote company, a four-person design studio operating exclusively from remote locations. The policy applies to all staff, contractors, and third parties with access to organisational information or systems. It covers all digital assets, devices, and data handling activities, regardless of physical location.

The Founder, Priya Shah, is responsible for information security governance and policy authorisation. All staff are accountable for complying with this policy. The Founder also holds the role of security responsible, ensuring that security controls are implemented and maintained across the organisation.

All user accounts must use multi-factor authentication (MFA). MFA is mandatory for all staff accounts and for all privileged accounts, including administrative access. Access to sensitive systems must be granted only to authorised personnel, with no exceptions. Privileged access must be separated from standard user access where feasible, and all privileged activities must be logged and reviewed.

All staff devices must be protected with endpoint protection software, which is currently in use. Devices must be patched regularly, and staff are responsible for applying updates promptly, including restarting devices after updates. Device encryption is required for all devices handling organisational data, and this control is currently unverified. Staff must ensure encryption is enabled on all work devices.

All confidential and personal information must be stored securely and accessed only by authorised personnel. Important business information must be backed up appropriately, with backups currently in place. Backups must be tested periodically to ensure recoverability. Data must not be stored on personal devices without encryption or explicit approval.

All work is conducted remotely. Staff must work from secure, private locations and must not share workspaces or devices with unauthorised individuals. Remote access to company systems must be secured through MFA and approved remote access control mechanisms. All staff are expected to maintain a secure and professional remote work environment.

Any suspected or actual security incident must be reported immediately to the Founder via the established incident reporting route. Staff must not delay reporting, even if they believe the issue is minor. All incidents must be documented and investigated promptly. No incident may be downgraded without review by the security responsible.

This policy is approved by the Founder, Priya Shah. It will be reviewed annually or sooner if significant changes occur in the organisation's operations, technology, or threat landscape. The current version is effective immediately. All staff must acknowledge and comply with this policy.

cases.title: Twenty-person London HQ + remote workers

sections.content: This Information Security Policy applies to all staff, contractors, and third parties who use or handle information assets within M004 policy-eval corpus - Twenty-person London HQ + remote workers. The policy ensures the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of organisational information across all work environments, including the London Head Office and remote working locations.

The Chief Operating Officer, Freya Lindqvist, is responsible for overseeing information security. All staff must comply with this policy and report any security concerns through the defined incident reporting route. The organisation maintains a clear governance structure with defined roles for security oversight and policy enforcement.

All user accounts must use multi-factor authentication (MFA). MFA is mandatory for all privileged accounts and all staff accounts. Access to systems must be granted only to authorised individuals, and privileged access must be separated from regular user access to prevent misuse. Account access must be revoked immediately upon staff departure or role change, and the joiner-mover-leaver process must be consistently applied.

All devices used for work must be encrypted. Devices must be kept up to date with all relevant software patches and updates. Endpoint protection must be in place across all devices, and any partial implementation must be fully remediated. Remote access must be secured via a mandatory, enforced VPN to ensure secure connections from any location.

All important business information must be backed up appropriately. Backups must be performed regularly and stored securely, with recovery procedures tested periodically. Confidential and personal information must be handled in accordance with organisational handling standards and retained only for as long as necessary.

Staff working remotely must use secure, encrypted connections and ensure their home workspace is physically secure. All remote access to organisational systems must be controlled through a mandatory, enforced VPN. Staff in the London Head Office must also follow secure practices, including device encryption and secure access controls.

Any suspected security incident must be reported immediately via the defined incident reporting route. Staff are expected to notify the responsible security lead without delay. The organisation has a confirmed incident reporting process in place to ensure timely response and remediation.

This policy is approved by the Chief Operating Officer, Freya Lindqvist. It will be reviewed annually or after any significant security event. Any changes to the policy must be documented and communicated to all relevant staff. The current version is effective immediately.

Systems with incomplete patching are subject to risk assessment and must be remediated.

All important business information must be backed up regularly and stored in a secure, accessible location. Backups must be tested at least quarterly to ensure recoverability. Backup data must be encrypted and protected from unauthorised access. Access to backup systems must be restricted to authorised personnel only.

Remote access to organisational systems must be secured through MFA and controlled via approved remote access tools. All remote work must be conducted using secure, approved devices and networks. Staff are required to notify the Operations Manager of any breach, suspicious activity, or potential compromise. Reporting must occur within 24 hours of discovery.
